newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Gold and diamonds boosted S.Africa trade data.
newsitem.headline: Gold and diamonds boosted S.Africa trade data.

text.p: Hefty South African gold and Botswana diamond exports were the main reasons for the sharp rise in the October trade surplus, figures released on Tuesday show.
But the statistics have been questioned by economists who say they do not tally with other official statistics.
Customs and Excise Department figures show South Africa exported three billion rand of gold in October, while Botswana exported 1.5 billion rand of diamonds.

The inclusion of these statistics was the main reason South Africa's trade surplus -- which includes statistics from Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia and Swaziland -- rocketed nearly 500 percent to 3.9 billion rand in the month.

A breakdown of the statistics, which was not provided with the department's official release of the data on Monday, was given by a Customs and Excise official on Tuesday, who said that both amounts were unusually high.
"Gold exports vary from 1.3 to 2.5 billion rand on a monthly basis, while Botswana diamonds which are included every two to three months are usually about 800 million rand."
The amount of gold exports translates into 53.57 tonnes -- 12 tonnes more than the country produced in October, according to Chamber of Mines data.
The official at Customs and Excise was unable to explain the sharp increase in gold exports, saying that the figures had been provided by the Reserve Bank.
A Reserve Bank official said there was no particular reason for the increase.
"The weakening of the rand obviously pushed up the price...but there was no particular reason."
South Africa's rand has depreciated nearly 30 percent against the dollar since February 15 this year.
Edward Osborn, strategic economist at Edey Rogers & Co, said he believed the discrepancy was an attempt to rectify past understatements of gold exports.
He believes that in recent years South African gold production has exceeded exports -- in 1994 by 2.6 billion rand and in 1995 by 3.3 billion rand.

"The essence of the matter is that because the definitions they (the Reserve Bank) have used in the balance of payments restricts the gold exports to the Bank's own sales, they have been ommitting the direct shipments of gold by the gold mining houses in closing out forward sales contracts," he said.
"They are now trying to correct past understatements."
The Customs and Excise official could also not comment on the virtual doubling in Botswana diamond exports.

The precious and semi-precious stones category of the statistics, which include both gold and diamonds, show exports rose to 5.8 billion rand in October, a 61 percent improvement on September's 3.6 billion rand.
Economists maintained that despite the anomalies, the trade surplus still held positive implications for the current account deficit in the fourth quarter of the year.
